paragraphs.title: The Command to Bring an Offering

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak in verse 1?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord spoke to Moses.”

easy.question: To whom was Moses told to speak in verse 2?
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Moses, “Speak to the Israelites.”

easy.question: What were the Israelites asked to bring to the Lord?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Let them bring me an offering.”

medium.question: Who was allowed to give the offering?
answers: Anyone who gave willingly from the heart
medium.explanation: The offering was to be taken from anyone whose heart moved him to give.

medium.question: What does “offering” mean in this context?
answers: A gift dedicated to the Lord
medium.explanation: The context shows that the people were to give a gift dedicated to the Lord.

medium.question: What is the order of communication in these verses?
answers: The Israelites speak to Moses, and Moses to the Lord
The Lord speaks to Moses, and Moses is told to speak to the Israelites
The priests speak to the Israelites, then to Moses
medium.explanation: First the Lord speaks to Moses, and then commands him to speak to the Israelites.

challenge.question: What do the words “whoever gives it willingly with his heart” show about giving?
answers: It had to be given secretly
It had to come from a willing heart
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that people were to give willingly, not merely under compulsion.

challenge.question: Why is Moses mentioned as the one who conveys the command to Israel?
answers: He serves as the mediator between the Lord and the people
He alone was allowed to give an offering
The Israelites did not know who they were
challenge.explanation: The Lord speaks to Moses and tells him to pass the command on to Israel, making Moses the messenger and mediator.

challenge.question: What is the likely meaning of “from every man” together with “who gives willingly”?
answers: Everyone had to give the same amount
Anyone who wished to could participate in giving
Only officials were allowed to give
challenge.explanation: The first phrase addresses everyone, while the second limits the offering to those moved to give.

questions.question: What do the words “whoever gives it willingly with his heart” show about giving?
answers: It had to be given secretly
It had to come from a willing heart
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that people were to give willingly, not merely under compulsion.

questions.question: Why is Moses mentioned as the one who conveys the command to Israel?
answers: He serves as the mediator between the Lord and the people
He alone was allowed to give an offering
The Israelites did not know who they were
questions.explanation: The Lord speaks to Moses and tells him to pass the command on to Israel, making Moses the messenger and mediator.

questions.question: What is the likely meaning of “from every man” together with “who gives willingly”?
answers: Everyone had to give the same amount
Anyone who wished to could participate in giving
Only officials were allowed to give
questions.explanation: The first phrase addresses everyone, while the second limits the offering to those moved to give.

easy.question: Which metals are mentioned in verse 3?
easy.explanation: The verse lists gold, silver, and bronze.

easy.question: What was the oil in verse 6 for?
easy.explanation: The verse specifically says, “Oil for the light.”

easy.question: Which stones are mentioned in verse 7?
answers: Onyx stones and stones to be set
easy.explanation: The verse mentions onyx stones and stones to be set in the ephod and breastplate.

medium.question: What does “offering” mean in “This is the offering which you shall take from them”?
answers: A gift or contribution for a specific purpose
A punishment taken from the people
medium.explanation: The people were giving materials for the construction of the sanctuary.

medium.question: What material was used for both anointing oil and sweet incense?
medium.explanation: Verse 6 mentions spices for anointing oil and for sweet incense.

medium.question: How can the materials in these verses be broadly grouped?
answers: As metals, fabrics, skins, wood, oils, spices, and stones
medium.explanation: The list includes many kinds of materials, including metals, fabrics, skins, wood, oils, spices, and stones.

challenge.question: What might we infer from the fact that both ordinary and valuable materials are listed?
answers: Only the priests had to contribute
The offering included many materials, so people could contribute what they had
The materials were intended only for trade
challenge.explanation: The varied list suggests that the offering was broad and diverse, allowing different kinds of contributions.

challenge.question: Which detail connects the stones with the priest’s clothing?
answers: The stones were for the ephod and breastplate
The stones were for building the altar
challenge.explanation: The verse says the stones were for the ephod and breastplate, parts of the priest’s garments.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the two uses of spices in verse 6?
answers: One was for lighting and one for making tools
One was for anointing oil and one for sweet incense
One was for dyeing skins and one for working wood
challenge.explanation: The spices were used to prepare anointing oil and sweet incense.

questions.question: What might we infer from the fact that both ordinary and valuable materials are listed?
answers: Only the priests had to contribute
The offering included many materials, so people could contribute what they had
The materials were intended only for trade
questions.explanation: The varied list suggests that the offering was broad and diverse, allowing different kinds of contributions.

questions.question: Which detail connects the stones with the priest’s clothing?
answers: The stones were for the ephod and breastplate
The stones were for building the altar
questions.explanation: The verse says the stones were for the ephod and breastplate, parts of the priest’s garments.

questions.question: What is the main difference between the two uses of spices in verse 6?
answers: One was for lighting and one for making tools
One was for anointing oil and one for sweet incense
One was for dyeing skins and one for working wood
questions.explanation: The spices were used to prepare anointing oil and sweet incense.

paragraphs.title: Building the Sanctuary According to the Pattern

easy.question: What were the Israelites commanded to make?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Let them make me a sanctuary.”

easy.question: What did the Lord promise after they made the sanctuary?
answers: To give them a new land
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “That I may dwell among them.”

easy.question: What was included in the pattern they were to follow?
answers: The tabernacle and all its furnishings
easy.explanation: The verse mentions both the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its furnishings.

medium.question: What is the connection between making the sanctuary and the Lord’s dwelling?
answers: The sanctuary was connected with the Lord dwelling among the people
The sanctuary was meant to replace the people
The sanctuary was made only for beauty
medium.explanation: The command to make the sanctuary is directly connected with the promise, “That I may dwell among them.”

medium.question: What does “pattern” mean in this context?
medium.explanation: The Lord showed Moses a model or plan according to which the tabernacle and its furnishings were to be made.

medium.question: What is the order of actions in these verses?
answers: They build first, and only afterward the Lord shows the plan
They dedicate the furnishings first, and then build
The Lord shows the plan, and then they make everything according to it
medium.explanation: The Lord first shows Moses the pattern and then commands, “So shall you make it.”

challenge.question: What can we understand from the words “among them” rather than “inside it”?
answers: The Lord would dwell among the people, not merely inside a building
The Lord would dwell only inside one furnishing
The Lord had no connection with the people
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes the Lord’s dwelling among the Israelites.

challenge.question: To whom is the command “So shall you make it” addressed?
answers: Only to the person who saw the plan
To those who were to build according to the pattern shown
Only to those who would carry the furnishings
challenge.explanation: The command tells the builders to make the tabernacle and its furnishings according to the model shown.

challenge.question: Which detail is easy to overlook in the description of the pattern?
answers: Only a general plan of the holy place is mentioned
Only a plan of the furnishings is mentioned
Both the tabernacle and all its furnishings are included
challenge.explanation: The verse separately mentions the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its furnishings.

questions.question: What can we understand from the words “among them” rather than “inside it”?
answers: The Lord would dwell among the people, not merely inside a building
The Lord would dwell only inside one furnishing
The Lord had no connection with the people
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes the Lord’s dwelling among the Israelites.

questions.question: To whom is the command “So shall you make it” addressed?
answers: Only to the person who saw the plan
To those who were to build according to the pattern shown
Only to those who would carry the furnishings
questions.explanation: The command tells the builders to make the tabernacle and its furnishings according to the model shown.

questions.question: Which detail is easy to overlook in the description of the pattern?
answers: Only a general plan of the holy place is mentioned
Only a plan of the furnishings is mentioned
Both the tabernacle and all its furnishings are included
questions.explanation: The verse separately mentions the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its furnishings.

paragraphs.title: Making the Ark of the Testimony

easy.question: What kind of wood was used to make the ark?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “They shall make an ark of shittim wood.”

easy.question: How long was the ark?
easy.explanation: The verse gives its length as two and a half cubits.

easy.question: With what was the ark overlaid?
easy.explanation: The ark was overlaid with pure gold within and without.

medium.question: What were the poles inserted into the ark’s rings for?
medium.explanation: The poles were used to carry the ark.

medium.question: What was done after the four gold rings were made for the ark?
answers: Poles were made of shittim wood and overlaid with gold
medium.explanation: The next instruction was to make poles of shittim wood and overlay them with gold.

medium.question: What does “poles” mean in this context?
medium.explanation: These were wooden poles placed in the rings so the ark could be carried.

challenge.question: What does the command “They shall not be taken from it” imply about the poles?
answers: They were to remain attached to the ark
They were not to be overlaid with gold
They had to be removed before carrying the ark
challenge.explanation: The poles were to remain in the ark’s rings and were not to be removed.

challenge.question: How were the four rings arranged on the ark?
answers: All four were on one side
Two were on each of its two sides
One was at each corner only
challenge.explanation: The verse specifies two rings on one side and two on the other.

challenge.question: What was to be placed inside the ark?
answers: The testimony that the Lord would give Moses
challenge.explanation: Verse 16 says to put in the ark the testimony that the Lord would give Moses.

questions.question: What does the command “They shall not be taken from it” imply about the poles?
answers: They were to remain attached to the ark
They were not to be overlaid with gold
They had to be removed before carrying the ark
questions.explanation: The poles were to remain in the ark’s rings and were not to be removed.

questions.question: How were the four rings arranged on the ark?
answers: All four were on one side
Two were on each of its two sides
One was at each corner only
questions.explanation: The verse specifies two rings on one side and two on the other.

questions.question: What was to be placed inside the ark?
answers: The testimony that the Lord would give Moses
questions.explanation: Verse 16 says to put in the ark the testimony that the Lord would give Moses.

paragraphs.title: The Mercy Seat and the Cherubim

easy.question: What was the mercy seat made of?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Make a mercy seat of pure gold.”

easy.question: How many cherubim were to be made?
easy.explanation: The command was to make two cherubim.

easy.question: Where was the mercy seat to be placed?
easy.explanation: The mercy seat was to be placed above the ark.

medium.question: What did the cherubim do with their wings?
medium.explanation: The cherubim stretched out their wings and covered the mercy seat.

medium.question: What does “of beaten work” mean here?
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the cherubim as made by shaping one piece of gold.

medium.question: What is the correct order according to the verses?
answers: The testimony was inside the ark, and the mercy seat was above it
The mercy seat was inside the ark, and the testimony above it
The cherubim were inside the ark, and the testimony beneath it
medium.explanation: The testimony was placed inside the ark, and the mercy seat was placed above it.

challenge.question: Which accurate description of the cherubim appears in the verses?
answers: Their wings were spread upward, and their faces looked toward each other and the mercy seat
Their wings were closed, and their faces looked outside the tabernacle
Their wings pointed downward, and their faces looked only at the ark
challenge.explanation: The cherubim had wings spread upward and faces turned toward each other and the mercy seat.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the dimensions of the mercy seat?
answers: Its width was greater than its length
Its length was one cubit greater than its width
Its length and width were equal
challenge.explanation: Its length was two and a half cubits and its width one and a half cubits, a difference of one cubit.

challenge.question: What was distinctive about how the cherubim were made?
answers: They were made of wood and overlaid with gold
They were placed separately from the mercy seat
They were made from the mercy seat itself, at its two ends
challenge.explanation: The cherubim were made from the mercy seat as part of it, at its two ends.

questions.question: Which accurate description of the cherubim appears in the verses?
answers: Their wings were spread upward, and their faces looked toward each other and the mercy seat
Their wings were closed, and their faces looked outside the tabernacle
Their wings pointed downward, and their faces looked only at the ark
questions.explanation: The cherubim had wings spread upward and faces turned toward each other and the mercy seat.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the dimensions of the mercy seat?
answers: Its width was greater than its length
Its length was one cubit greater than its width
Its length and width were equal
questions.explanation: Its length was two and a half cubits and its width one and a half cubits, a difference of one cubit.

questions.question: What was distinctive about how the cherubim were made?
answers: They were made of wood and overlaid with gold
They were placed separately from the mercy seat
They were made from the mercy seat itself, at its two ends
questions.explanation: The cherubim were made from the mercy seat as part of it, at its two ends.

paragraphs.title: The Lord Speaks from Above the Mercy Seat

easy.question: Where would the Lord speak with Moses?
answers: Above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim
easy.explanation: The Lord would speak with Moses from above the mercy seat, between the cherubim.

easy.question: With whom did the Lord say He would speak?
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “There I will meet with you.”

easy.question: What would Moses convey to the Israelites?
easy.explanation: Moses was to pass on everything the Lord commanded him.

medium.question: What does “There I will meet with you” mean?
answers: I will meet with you there
I will send you away from there
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a meeting place where the Lord would speak with Moses.

medium.question: What arrangement of the sacred objects is described?
answers: The cherubim are between the mercy seat and the ark
The mercy seat is beneath the ark
The cherubim are on the mercy seat, and the mercy seat is on the ark of the testimony
medium.explanation: The cherubim are on the mercy seat, which is placed above the ark of the testimony.

medium.question: What can we understand from the Lord speaking with Moses and commanding him to address Israel?
answers: Moses serves as the messenger who conveys the Lord’s words
Moses has no role in conveying the command
medium.explanation: The Lord speaks to Moses, who then passes the instructions on to Israel.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that the divine speech is connected with a specific holy place?
answers: The mention of the mercy seat, cherubim, and ark of the testimony
challenge.explanation: The sacred objects identify the holy place where the meeting would occur.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the transition between “I will commune with you” and “which I will give you in commandment unto the children of Israel”?
answers: The words were intended only for Moses
Moses would receive the command and pass it on to the people
The Israelites would hear the Lord directly at that moment
challenge.explanation: Moses is presented as the one who receives the Lord’s command and delivers it to Israel.

challenge.question: What is the precise distinction between “above the mercy seat” and “above the ark of the testimony”?
answers: The speech took place outside the ark
The mercy seat is above the ark, and the speech is described as taking place above the mercy seat
challenge.explanation: The ark supports the mercy seat, so the place of speech is described as above the mercy seat.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that the divine speech is connected with a specific holy place?
answers: The mention of the mercy seat, cherubim, and ark of the testimony
questions.explanation: The sacred objects identify the holy place where the meeting would occur.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the transition between “I will commune with you” and “which I will give you in commandment unto the children of Israel”?
answers: The words were intended only for Moses
Moses would receive the command and pass it on to the people
The Israelites would hear the Lord directly at that moment
questions.explanation: Moses is presented as the one who receives the Lord’s command and delivers it to Israel.

questions.question: What is the precise distinction between “above the mercy seat” and “above the ark of the testimony”?
answers: The speech took place outside the ark
The mercy seat is above the ark, and the speech is described as taking place above the mercy seat
questions.explanation: The ark supports the mercy seat, so the place of speech is described as above the mercy seat.

paragraphs.title: Making the Table for the Showbread

easy.question: What were they commanded to make in these verses?
easy.explanation: These verses describe the making of the table.

easy.question: What was the table overlaid with?
easy.explanation: The table was overlaid with pure gold.

easy.question: How many gold rings were to be made for the table?
easy.explanation: The command was to make four gold rings for it.

medium.question: What were the rings and poles for?
medium.explanation: The poles were placed in the rings so the table could be carried.

medium.question: What does “border” mean in “a border of a handbreadth round about”?
answers: A rim or frame around the table
medium.explanation: The context indicates a rim surrounding the table.

medium.question: Why were the poles also overlaid with gold?
answers: To match the appearance of the gold-covered table
To serve as the table’s legs
medium.explanation: The gold-covered poles matched the table’s special design.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the command to make rings and poles for the table?
answers: The table was fixed to the floor
The table was meant for sitting
The table was portable and could be carried
challenge.explanation: The rings and poles were specifically made for carrying the table.

challenge.question: What is the correct order for making the table?
answers: Make it of wood, overlay it with gold, and add rings and poles
Make the poles, place them on the table, and then build it
Overlay it with gold, take it apart, and add legs
challenge.explanation: The instructions first call for wooden construction, then gold overlay, followed by the rings and poles.

challenge.question: Where were the rings placed according to the description?
answers: At the four corners near its four feet
In the center of the tabletop
Only on one side of the table
challenge.explanation: The rings were placed at the four corners by the four feet so the table could be carried securely.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the command to make rings and poles for the table?
answers: The table was fixed to the floor
The table was meant for sitting
The table was portable and could be carried
questions.explanation: The rings and poles were specifically made for carrying the table.

questions.question: What is the correct order for making the table?
answers: Make it of wood, overlay it with gold, and add rings and poles
Make the poles, place them on the table, and then build it
Overlay it with gold, take it apart, and add legs
questions.explanation: The instructions first call for wooden construction, then gold overlay, followed by the rings and poles.

questions.question: Where were the rings placed according to the description?
answers: At the four corners near its four feet
In the center of the tabletop
Only on one side of the table
questions.explanation: The rings were placed at the four corners by the four feet so the table could be carried securely.

paragraphs.title: The Table’s Utensils and the Showbread

easy.question: What were the utensils in verse 29 to be made of?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Of pure gold shall you make them.”

easy.question: What was to be placed on the table?
easy.explanation: Verse 30 commands that showbread be set on the table.

easy.question: Before whom was the bread to remain continually?
easy.explanation: The verse says the bread was to be continually before the Lord.

medium.question: Why are both the utensils and the bread mentioned here?
answers: To describe the construction of the altar
medium.explanation: The utensils belonged to the table, and showbread was to be placed on it.

medium.question: What are the “covers” and other items in the table’s list?
answers: Utensils or accessories for the table
medium.explanation: They are listed as equipment to be made for use with the table.

medium.question: What is the connection between making the utensils and placing the showbread?
answers: The utensils were connected with the bread served on the table
The bread was used to make the utensils
medium.explanation: The utensils are described first, followed by the command to place bread on the table.

challenge.question: Which word shows that the showbread was not placed on the table only occasionally?
challenge.explanation: The word “always” shows that the bread was to remain continually before the Lord.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from requiring all the utensils to be made of pure gold?
answers: The table was for a private meal
The table’s service was considered holy and honorable
The bread was made of gold
challenge.explanation: Pure gold emphasizes the importance and holiness of the table’s service.

challenge.question: Which wording shows that the bread was placed on the table, not inside one of the utensils?
challenge.explanation: The phrase “upon the table” clearly places the bread on top of it.

questions.question: Which word shows that the showbread was not placed on the table only occasionally?
questions.explanation: The word “always” shows that the bread was to remain continually before the Lord.

questions.question: What can be inferred from requiring all the utensils to be made of pure gold?
answers: The table was for a private meal
The table’s service was considered holy and honorable
The bread was made of gold
questions.explanation: Pure gold emphasizes the importance and holiness of the table’s service.

questions.question: Which wording shows that the bread was placed on the table, not inside one of the utensils?
questions.explanation: The phrase “upon the table” clearly places the bread on top of it.

easy.question: What was the lampstand to be made of?
easy.explanation: The verse commands, “Make a lampstand of pure gold.”

easy.question: What object is described in this verse?
easy.explanation: The verse gives instructions for making the lampstand.

easy.question: What is said about the bowls, knobs, and flowers?
answers: They were to be made of wood
They were separate from the lampstand
They were to be part of the lampstand itself
easy.explanation: The verse says they were to be made from the same piece as the lampstand.

medium.question: What can we understand from the statement that the lampstand and its parts were “of the same”?
answers: The parts were made as part of the lampstand, not separately
The lampstand stood outside the tabernacle
The lampstand was made of several metals
medium.explanation: The shaft, branches, bowls, knobs, and flowers were all part of one lampstand.

medium.question: What does “of beaten work” mean in this verse?
answers: A lampstand shaped from one piece of metal
medium.explanation: The expression describes shaping the lampstand by hammering or working one piece of gold.

medium.question: Which part is mentioned before the branches and bowls?
medium.explanation: The verse lists the shaft and branches before the bowls, knobs, and flowers.

challenge.question: What combination of material and method is correct?
challenge.explanation: The verse specifies both pure gold and beaten work.

challenge.question: What does “of the same” emphasize about the bowls, knobs, and flowers?
answers: They were integrated parts of the lampstand
They were placed beside it separately
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that the parts were formed from and integrated into the lampstand.

challenge.question: Which detail appears explicitly in the verse?
answers: The lampstand was lit every evening
The lampstand stood at the tabernacle entrance
Its shaft and branches were part of the lampstand
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions the shaft and branches as parts of the lampstand.

questions.question: What combination of material and method is correct?
questions.explanation: The verse specifies both pure gold and beaten work.

questions.question: What does “of the same” emphasize about the bowls, knobs, and flowers?
answers: They were integrated parts of the lampstand
They were placed beside it separately
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that the parts were formed from and integrated into the lampstand.

questions.question: Which detail appears explicitly in the verse?
answers: The lampstand was lit every evening
The lampstand stood at the tabernacle entrance
Its shaft and branches were part of the lampstand
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions the shaft and branches as parts of the lampstand.

paragraphs.title: The Six Branches Extending from the Lampstand

easy.question: How many branches came out from the sides of the lampstand?
easy.explanation: The verse says that six branches came out from its sides.

easy.question: How many branches were on each side?
easy.explanation: There were three branches on each side.

easy.question: How many almond-shaped bowls were on each branch?
easy.explanation: Each branch had three almond-shaped bowls.

medium.question: How were the six branches divided between the two sides?
medium.explanation: The verse specifies three branches on one side and three on the other.

medium.question: What does “made like almonds” describe?
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the shape of the bowls.

medium.question: What repeated design appeared on each of the six branches?
answers: Three bowls, a knob, and a flower
medium.explanation: Each branch had three almond-shaped bowls, a knob, and a flower.

challenge.question: How many almond-shaped bowls were there altogether on the six branches?
challenge.explanation: There were three bowls on each of six branches: 6 × 3 = 18.

challenge.question: What does “so” mean in “so in the six branches”?
answers: The same design on all six branches
challenge.explanation: It applies the pattern just described to all six branches.

challenge.question: What feature of the lampstand’s design stands out?
answers: The two sides were balanced and repeated the same design
challenge.explanation: Each side had three branches, and the same decorative pattern was repeated.

questions.question: How many almond-shaped bowls were there altogether on the six branches?
questions.explanation: There were three bowls on each of six branches: 6 × 3 = 18.

questions.question: What does “so” mean in “so in the six branches”?
answers: The same design on all six branches
questions.explanation: It applies the pattern just described to all six branches.

questions.question: What feature of the lampstand’s design stands out?
answers: The two sides were balanced and repeated the same design
questions.explanation: Each side had three branches, and the same decorative pattern was repeated.

paragraphs.title: The Bowls and Knobs of the Lampstand and Branches

easy.question: How many bowls were on the lampstand itself?
easy.explanation: The verse says there were four bowls on the lampstand.

easy.question: How many branches came out from the lampstand?
easy.explanation: The passage describes six branches extending from the lampstand.

easy.question: What was the lampstand made of?
easy.explanation: The passage says it was one beaten work of pure gold.

medium.question: What was beneath each pair of branches?
medium.explanation: The verse repeatedly says that a knob was beneath each pair of branches.

medium.question: What does “made like almonds” describe?
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the decorative almond-like shape of the bowls.

medium.question: What does “of the same” mean in “their knobs and their branches shall be of the same”?
answers: The knobs and branches were part of the lampstand
The knobs were placed only beside the lampstand
The branches were made of another material
medium.explanation: The wording shows that the knobs and branches were formed as parts of the lampstand.

challenge.question: How many knobs were beneath the pairs of branches?
challenge.explanation: Six branches formed three pairs, with one knob beneath each pair.

challenge.question: What does “one beaten work” emphasize?
answers: The lampstand was made of separate pieces
The lampstand was made as one unit
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the lampstand was formed as one piece rather than assembled from separate parts.

challenge.question: Which statement correctly combines the details in these verses?
answers: There were four bowls, six branches, and three knobs
There were six bowls, four branches, and two knobs
There were three bowls, six branches, and four knobs
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions four bowls, six branches, and three knobs—one beneath each pair of branches.

questions.question: How many knobs were beneath the pairs of branches?
questions.explanation: Six branches formed three pairs, with one knob beneath each pair.

questions.question: What does “one beaten work” emphasize?
answers: The lampstand was made of separate pieces
The lampstand was made as one unit
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the lampstand was formed as one piece rather than assembled from separate parts.

questions.question: Which statement correctly combines the details in these verses?
answers: There were four bowls, six branches, and three knobs
There were six bowls, four branches, and two knobs
There were three bowls, six branches, and four knobs
questions.explanation: The passage mentions four bowls, six branches, and three knobs—one beneath each pair of branches.

paragraphs.title: The Seven Lamps and Their Utensils

easy.question: How many lamps did the lampstand have?
easy.explanation: The verse commands that it have seven lamps.

easy.question: What were the tongs and snuffdishes made of?

paragraphs.title: The Pattern Shown on the Mountain

easy.question: What did the Lord command Moses to do?
easy.explanation: The verse commands, “Look that you make them.”

easy.question: Where did the Lord show Moses these things?
easy.explanation: The verse says the pattern was shown to Moses on the mountain.

easy.question: According to what was Moses to make them?
answers: According to the pattern shown by the Lord
easy.explanation: Moses was to make them according to the pattern shown to him.

medium.question: Why did Moses need to see the pattern before making the furnishings?
answers: So he could follow the model shown to him
So he would know when to leave the mountain
So he could find water in the wilderness
medium.explanation: Seeing the pattern gave Moses the model according to which he was to make everything.

medium.question: What does “after their pattern” mean in this verse?
answers: According to their design or form
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Moses was to follow the design or form shown to him.

medium.question: What is the order of actions in the verse?
answers: Leave the mountain and then make
medium.explanation: The instruction first refers to what Moses was shown and then tells him to make the objects accordingly.

Moses was forbidden to make anything
challenge.explanation: Following the pattern indicates that the work had to be done according to a precise model.

challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the pattern that the Lord showed Moses on the mountain.

challenge.explanation: The direct address “you” shows that Moses was the one who had seen the pattern and was responsible for making the furnishings.
